title: CI runs at milestones, not on every merge, and you get options on best practice
why: Your gripe, Oct 27 (waiting page, item 27): "Not only drop the exception, I merge so arbitrarily and can merge so often that frankly I still find the amount of CI used to be preposterous. I think there may be something in this roadmap already of essentially wanting \"milestone-style\" reviews of CI -- I think my Q_Max repo might have some examples of that where I got so sick of my CI bill that I was like look orchestrator after u see a ton has landed then yes run a check but not every merge. That could be me not doing best practices, and I'm eager to learn, and/but I want some help here"
note: No earlier step covers it (checked roadmap d0c17e61; c39, CI time caps, is done and about caps, not volume). Item 27 (c69) answered a: drop the per-lane full CI job exception; the build advisor (6) has it. The example you mean: q_max D-695 (checks run in tiers: narrow on a branch, full on main) and its full browser suite on main only, on dispatch. Part 1, needs no answer: a short options write-up, each with a gold-standard column: what runs per lane, per batch, per merge to main and per milestone; what each catches and costs in CI minutes (measured from claude-settings' Actions history); where q_max and degen (one test run per batch) already sit; and a pick. Part 2, deferred (shiv, Oct 27): you choose; the rule lands in the global CLAUDE.md (rule roles-each-layer-proves-once, git-integration-branch-merge) and the gates workflows. Port: yes; the rule is global, each repo's workflows follow at its visit. Placed after c88, ahead of c82 (triage, Oct 27): CI spend grows with every merge.
